ălĭquotfărĭam , adv. prop. acc. fem.; cf. bi- quadri- multi- omni-fariam,
I.in some or several places: “In eo (Picentium) agro aliquotfariam in singula jugera dena cullea vini fiunt,” Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 7 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
